The creatures that inhabit the world of *Pokémon* are also called Pokémon.[[2]](#cite_note-TIME-2) The word "Pokémon" is a [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Japanese "Romanization of Japanese") [contraction](/wiki/Contraction_(grammar) "Contraction (grammar)") of the Japanese brand Pocket Monsters (ポケットモンスター, *Poketto Monsutā*).[[3]](#cite_note-NYT1-3) The concept of the Pokémon universe, in both the video games and the general fictional world of Pokémon, stems most notably from Tajiri's childhood hobby of [insect collecting](/wiki/Insect_collecting "Insect collecting"). Other influences on the concept include [Ultraman](/wiki/Ultraman_(1966_TV_series) "Ultraman (1966 TV series)"), [anime](/wiki/Anime "Anime"), and playing video games in general. Throughout his early life, Tajiri saw his rural, nature-filled hometown transform into an urban centre. The urbanization of his town drove away wildlife, and he and others living in the area were eventually unable to collect insects. Through Pokémon, Tajiri sought to bring back this outdoor pastime and share it with the world.[[2]](#cite_note-TIME-2) The first games in the franchise, [*Red* and *Green*](/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue "Pokémon Red and Blue"), were released on 27 February 1996 in Japan for the [Game Boy](/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy").[[4]](#cite_note-4) The games were internationally released as *Red* and *Blue* in September 1998.[[5]](#cite_note-5) The ability to capture, battle, trade, and care for numerous creatures catapulted Pokémon to international popularity,[[3]](#cite_note-NYT1-3) and it has become a multibillion-dollar franchise and the second-best selling video game series after the [Mario franchise](/wiki/Mario_(franch

**Australia**, officially the **Commonwealth of Australia**, is a country comprising the [mainland](/wiki/Mainland_Australia "Mainland Australia") of the [Australian continent](/wiki/Australia_(continent) "Australia (continent)"), the island of [Tasmania](/wiki/Tasmania "Tasmania") and [numerous smaller islands](/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Australia "List of islands of Australia").[[N 6]](#cite_note-22) It has a land area of 7,688,287 km2 (2,968,464 sq mi), making it the [sixth-largest country in the world](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area"). Australia is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.
